purpose: Integrate separately authored Operation value compositions and Workflow call closure into complete native TypeScript project planning. No files or providers execute during planning.
selection: The v2 selection retains the explicit v1 module layout, exact value profile, field bindings, validators, effect actions and Workflow occurrence bindings. It adds value_compositions, exactly one per Operation, each with a closed composition and explicit absence_failures. An empty binding list represents an Operation with no named value calls. Missing, duplicate, stale or extra selections reject.
checking: All nodes share one compiled graph, composition boundary and exact field model. Check each named call, effect action, guard, Event and result. Compile Workflow calls against full composed action identities and their finite precommit settlement vocabulary. Existing source occurrence ordering and recovery semantics remain unchanged.
resolution: An explicit v2 resolved selection admits composed-operations and composed-workflows in addition to existing generator requests. Only registered checked objects are consumed. Preserve existing path safety, definition byte bindings, exact artifact content hashes, duplicate byte deduplication, collision rejection and native import/export resolution. Legacy v1 entry points reject these request kinds.
coverage: Generate every supported project node using its selected native generator. Every project node must have a represented module. Shared and transitive imports must resolve to the emitted artifact set; dependencies cannot be omitted to make a project pass. Root selection projects exact checked artifact bytes, not a second compilation path.
compatibility: Additive opt-in v2 selection and entry points only. Closed v1 selection decoding, legacy checked action ownership and old contract bytes remain unchanged. No hidden defaults, arbitrary callbacks, runtime graph interpreter, publication or provider execution are introduced.
limitations: This candidate is TypeScript project planning and artifact selection, not cross-language parity, Alch source integration, installed CLI verification, provider durability or whole-application readiness.
